chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man owns his parents, or his sister, or his paternal aunt, or his maternal aunt, they are emancipated; and he may own the son of his brother, and his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle; and he may own his brother, and his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle through the breastfeeding relationship.

key_terms.الرَّضَاعَةِ: rida'/breastfeeding — the foster-nursing relationship that creates quasi-kinship in Islamic law
key_terms.عَتَقُوا: they are emancipated — automatic legal emancipation upon ownership
key_terms.وَالِدَيْهِ: both parents (father and mother) — dual form indicating both parents are included

ai.seo_question: Which relatives are automatically emancipated if a man owns them in Islamic law according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a key jurisprudential rule regarding slavery and family emancipation: certain close female and maternal relatives — parents, sister, paternal aunt, and maternal aunt — are automatically freed if a man comes to own them as slaves. The ruling reflects Islamic law's recognition that ownership of certain blood relatives is incompatible with family sanctity. In contrast, male-line relatives (nephew, paternal uncle, maternal uncle) and relatives through the foster-nursing (rida') relationship do not receive automatic emancipation and may remain in ownership. This distinction between categories of relatives illustrates the jurisprudence of emancipation in classical Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man owns his parents, or his sister, or his paternal aunt, or his maternal aunt, they would be emancipated (liberated), and he can own a son of his brother, and his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle, and he can own his brother, and his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle from the breast-feeding (relationship)’.
